content.text:
**Your diagnosis is supported by the code: billing is centralized in Not Organic, but each service still interprets Pro access separately. Your admin status currently does not automatically grant Pro across them.**

For Twyne specifically:

- **New Pro signup is currently closed.** I checked the [live pricing page](https://www.twyne.love/pricing/): its button says “New subscriptions available soon.”
- **An existing Not Organic Twyne subscription should connect through sign-in.** Twyne links your verified Not Organic account, reads its wallet, and checks the subscription there. It currently requires exactly `twyne_pro_v2`, status `active`, and an unexpired billing period. [Access check](/home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne/src/utils/subscription-plan.ts:8)
- There is no general “attach any existing Pro subscription” mechanism in that path. A subscription belonging to another product or another Not Organic account will not unlock Twyne.

The separation currently works like this:

- **Identity:** your Not Organic account connects your accounts across services.
- **Subscriptions:** product-specific access. Twyne Pro does not automatically grant Interleave Pro or a Stich plan.
- **Credits:** shared AI spending funds. Most paid subscription allowances and credit packs are usable across services; some grants are restricted, such as Interleave’s free allowance. Purchased packs do not expire; the listed monthly allowances generally roll over for one billing cycle. [Credit catalog](/home/diogenes/Projects/apps/notorganic-provider/packages/core/src/grants.ts:3)
- **Admin:** a separate permission system. Not Organic checks an administrator account list; Twyne also maintains its own admin roster. Neither is connected to Twyne’s Pro check.

For example, **Twyne Pro includes $10 of shared AI credit, but spending that credit in another service does not grant that service’s paid features.** Conversely, buying $25 of credit does not grant Twyne Pro.

There are concrete inconsistencies behind the disconnect:

- Twyne accepts only its current plan and `active` status; Interleave accepts several plan aliases and also `paid`/`trialing`.
- Twyne’s check excludes the legacy `twyne_pro` plan even though Not Organic retains that catalog entry.
- Each app has separate checkout configuration gates.
- The Not Organic portal displays subscriptions but directs users back to individual products for purchases and plan changes. [Portal behavior](/home/diogenes/Projects/apps/notorganic-provider/apps/portal/src/views/Settings.tsx:332)

**Your admin account should receive centrally granted Pro access across these services.** The coherent implementation is for Not Organic to return each product’s effective access, including whether it comes from a paid subscription or an admin grant. Every app should consume that result. AI spending should remain separately accounted for, with an explicit admin-funded budget.

I inspected source and Twyne’s public page; I did not inspect your private account, complete a payment, or change access. The missing admin-to-Pro behavior is confirmed in Twyne’s code.
